heading: Smart energy and water efficiency pilot program

children.heading: Eligible entity
children.text: The term “eligible entity” means—
a utility;
a municipality;
a water district;
an Indian Tribe or Alaska Native village; and
any other authority that provides water, wastewater, or water reuse services.

children.heading: Smart energy and water efficiency pilot program
children.text: The term “smart energy and water efficiency pilot program” or “pilot program” means the pilot program established under subsection (b).

tree.heading: Smart energy and water efficiency pilot program

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Secretary shall establish and carry out a smart energy and water efficiency pilot program in accordance with this section.

children.heading: Purpose
children.text: The purpose of the smart energy and water efficiency pilot program is to award grants to eligible entities to demonstrate unique, advanced, or innovative technology-based solutions that will—
improve the net energy balance of water, wastewater, and water reuse systems;

improve the net energy balance of water, wastewater, and water reuse systems to help communities across the United States make measurable progress in conserving water, saving energy, and reducing costs;
support the implementation of innovative and unique processes and the installation of established advanced automated systems that provide real-time data on energy and water; and

improve energy-water conservation and quality and predictive maintenance through technologies that utilize internet connected technologies, including sensors, intelligent gateways, and security embedded in hardware.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Secretary shall make competitive, merit-reviewed grants under the pilot program to not less than 3, but not more than 5, eligible entities.

children.heading: Selection criteria
children.text: In selecting an eligible entity to receive a grant under the pilot program, the Secretary shall consider—
energy and cost savings;
the uniqueness, commercial viability, and reliability of the technology to be used;
the degree to which the project integrates next-generation sensors software, analytics, and management tools;
the anticipated cost-effectiveness of the pilot project through measurable energy savings, water savings or reuse, and infrastructure costs averted;

whether the technology can be deployed in a variety of geographic regions and the degree to which the technology can be implemented in a wide range of applications ranging in scale from small towns to large cities, including Tribal communities;
whether the technology has been successfully deployed elsewhere;
whether the technology was sourced from a manufacturer based in the United States; and
whether the project will be completed in 5 years or less.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to clause (ii), an eligible entity seeking a grant under the pilot program shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary determines to be necessary.

children.heading: Contents
children.text: An application under clause (i) shall, at a minimum, include—
a description of the project;
a description of the technology to be used in the project;
the anticipated results, including energy and water savings, of the project;
a comprehensive budget for the project;
the names of the project lead organization and any partners;
the number of users to be served by the project;
a description of the ways in which the proposal would meet performance measures established by the Secretary; and
any other information that the Secretary determines to be necessary to complete the review and selection of a grant recipient.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Not later than 1 year after December 27, 2020, the Secretary shall select grant recipients under this section.

children.heading: Annual evaluations
children.text: The Secretary shall annually carry out an evaluation of each project for which a grant is provided under this section that meets performance measures and benchmarks developed by the Secretary, consistent with the purposes of this section.

children.heading: Requirements
children.text: Consistent with the performance measures and benchmarks developed under clause (i), in carrying out an evaluation under that clause, the Secretary shall—
evaluate the progress and impact of the project; and
assess the degree to which the project is meeting the goals of the pilot program.

children.heading: Technical and policy assistance
children.text: On the request of a grant recipient, the Secretary shall provide technical and policy assistance.

children.heading: Best practices
children.text: The Secretary shall make available to the public through the Internet and other means the Secretary considers to be appropriate—
a copy of each evaluation carried out under subparagraph (B); and
a description of any best practices identified by the Secretary as a result of those evaluations.

children.heading: Report to Congress
children.text: The Secretary shall submit to Congress a report containing the results of each evaluation carried out under subparagraph (B).

tree.heading: Authorization of appropriations
tree.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $15,000,000, to remain available until expended.
